newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WMC sees May 8 Kalgoorlie smelter restart.
newsitem.headline: WMC sees May 8 Kalgoorlie smelter restart.

text.p: WMC Ltd said on Thursday that it expected to resume production from its Kalgoorlie nickel smelter in Western Australia on May 8.
The smelter has been closed since April 6 when part of the flash furnace roof collapsed.
WMC said production from its Kambalda, Leinster and Mt Keith mining operations had not been affected by the closure and the impact on concentrate production was expected to be minimal.
The company said earlier that it would use the enforced enclosure to bring forward planned four days of maintenance work set for May and a 14-day shutdown scheduled for October.
WMC said it hoped the rescheduling would mean a loss in annual nickel matte production of only 3,000 tonnes rather than the 7,000 tonnes which would normally be lost from a 30 day smelter shutdown.

It also said production from the Kwinana nickel refinery in Western Australia was expected to fall by about 3,000 tonnes in during this shutdown period, with the refinery using matte stocks and concentrate from Mt Keith to continue operations at a reduced rate.
